videos.title: The AI Billing Stack for Healthcare
videos.description:
Candid Health is rebuilding the medical billing stack for healthcare providers, automating the work required to get claims submitted correctly and providers paid. 

Medical billing is a $200–300 billion market, and much of it still runs on decades-old software and manual processes. Today, Candid serves more than 200 healthcare organizations, processes about $7 billion in claims each year, and recently raised a $120 million Series D to keep expanding into the broader healthcare market.

In this Founder Fireside, co-founder and CEO Nick Perry joins YC's Gustaf Alströmer to share how Candid went from manually reviewing every claim to building the automation layer behind the business. He also explains where AI and agents fit into medical billing, and why the goal is to prevent denials before they happen.

Chapters:
00:00 — What Candid Health Does
00:26 — Why Medical Billing Is So Complicated
02:13 — How Medical Claims Actually Work
07:27 — The $300B Medical Billing Market
09:14 — Finding Candid’s Wedge
11:00 — Winning the First Customer
13:00 — Doing Things That Don’t Scale
15:33 — Automating RCM With Software and AI
17:55 — From Palantir to Candid Health
19:25 — The Moment They Hit Product-Market Fit
20:44 — Building the Team and Culture
23:39 — From the First 10 Customers to Scale
27:24 — Where AI Agents Matter Most
30:14 — Raising a Series D and What Comes Next
37:33 — The Startup Lesson Nick Wishes He Knew

videos.title: How Anthropic ships the #1 LLM in the World — with Katelyn Lesse and Angela Jiang
videos.description:
An agent’s sandbox can die without taking the whole agent with it. That’s the idea behind “the brain and the hands,” Anthropic’s architecture for Claude Managed Agents.

Now that the dust has settled on Opus 5.5, it is universally agreed to be the best model in the world. In this conversation with Katelyn Lesse and Angela Jiang, Anthropic’s Heads of Engineering and of Product, goes inside the systems that turn model capabilities into products developers can use.

We cover:

- Why Anthropic separated the agent harness, session state and execution environment.
- Letting agents use credentials without putting those credentials inside their sandboxes.
- Rebuilding the Messages API from Python to Rust with Claude—and verifying the rewrite with shadow traffic.
- Preventing model distillation while preserving the developer experience.
- Memory, “dreaming,” agent evaluations and the work still left for human engineers.
- How Anthropic’s own teams use Claude while keeping responsibility for their code and writing.

The episode opens with swyx’s look at Anthropic’s S-1: revenue per employee, compute efficiency, and the improvement and investment loops behind the business.

**Related links**

- [Claude Opus 5.5](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5) — Performance, pricing and safeguards.
- [The brain and the hands](https://www.anthropic.com/research/managed-agents) — The Managed Agents architecture.
- [How Anthropic contains Claude](https://www.anthropic.com/research/how-we-contain-claude) — Isolation, credentials and network controls.
- [Harnesses for long-running agents](https://www.anthropic.com/research/effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents) — Maintaining progress across context windows.

videos.title: An Eval for AI Scientists That Knows the Answer Key - Ian Quigley, Leash Bio
videos.description:
Leash Biosciences built a platform to physically measure thousands of proteins against millions of molecules. In this followup to our Leash Bio podcast with cofounder Ian Quigley, he returns to discuss the release of Minos, Leash’s framework of pre-measured experimental worlds that scientific agents can explore. 

Ian goes into how scientific agents traverse these environments, whether they use information from prior experiments to inform future choices, how good they get at medicinal chemistry, and how their broad decision making abilities affect their performance. 

We cover:
- Huge action spaces that can be explored by reasoning agents
- Which models are the best at medicinal chemistry
- What mistakes they make and how Leash can tell
- How agents weren’t ready to do this at all a year ago
- The basic idea of a lab-in-the-loop with zero latency
- The path to large numbers of new worlds

Leash published this work and is releasing a few dozen Minos worlds and thousands of agent transcripts for the community to use.

Original YouTube with Ian Quigley: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hQSBJVreLms
Blog post: https://leashbio.substack.com/p/making-reality-replayable
Preprint: https://github.com/Leash-Labs/minos-paper/blob/trunk/Minos_Leash.pdf
Data and transcripts: https://strelka.leash.bio/
